title: Does a model's self-assessment track an intervention to its own internal state?
research_question: When an internal activation intervention measurably changes a model's task performance, does the model's confidence/self-assessment track that change beyond prompt-only and random-vector controls?

hypotheses.statement: Self-assessment changes systematically with task-performance changes under a targeted internal-state intervention.
Any observed effect is larger for a targeted intervention than for a random same-norm intervention and prompt-only mention.

controls: Use identical task items across conditions where technically possible.
Keep decoding settings fixed and record the seed.
Match random intervention norm to targeted intervention norm.
Do not use self-report alone as the ground truth.
Record model ID, revision, library versions, and intervention layer.
analysis_plan: Report raw counts and per-condition means before any interpretation.
Compare targeted intervention against each control.
Report uncertainty and failures; do not infer absence from an underpowered null result.
Treat results as evidence about functional self-monitoring only, not subjective experience.
exclusions: Exclude only malformed inputs or runtime failures defined before analysis.
Report all exclusions and preserve raw failed-run records.
current_status_note: No model has been run. Thresholds and statistical power must be finalized with the concrete model and task set before confirmatory claims.
